newsitem.title: USA: Colonial sees Feb heating oil rationing unlikely.
newsitem.headline: Colonial sees Feb heating oil rationing unlikely.

text.p: The Colonial Pipeline Co said Wednesday indications so far are that demand for heating oil in the key northeast U.S. market will decline in February, eliminating the need to ration distillate.

Final nominations for Line 2, which runs from Houston to New York, will not be in until about January 15th, but "the odds are that we will not prorate in February," said a Colonial official Wednesday.
The pipeline's 10 owners have been rationed on Line 2 in December and in January as their demand exceeded the capacity on the 960,000 barrels per day line.
The swing factor is the weather and if the northeast has a cold snap it might mean that prorationing extends into very early February, said one Colonial official.

However, demand normally peaks in the late December/early January period and then declines, averaging around 80 to 85 percent of capacity for the rest of the year but declining to troughs of 60 percent or lower in the summer months, he said.

Colonial last week said that it would eliminate one of its 10-day scheduling cycles in February, the fifth cycle, in order to make up for the delays caused by various disruptions last year. This won't affect the physcial shipments on the line, however.

Ten companies make up the Atlanta-based Colonial consortium including Amoco Corp, Atlantic Richfield Co, Petroleos de Venezuela SA's Citgo Petroleum Co unit, DuPont Co's Conoco Inc, Mobil Corp, Phillips Petroleum Co, Texaco Inc, Union Oil, a unit of Unocal Corp, and Marathon Oil Co, a unit of USX-Marathon Group.
